title: Choose CareCommand’s new Today workspace
question: All three keep CareCommand’s trusted clinical identity. Choose how a practice manager should understand and run the day.

options.label: Operational Briefing
options.lineage: A concise shift briefing that opens into accountable work
options.thesis: Start with what changed, what is at risk, and the three actions that will stabilize the day.
options.viewport: A network-and-clinic scope bar leads into a morning brief, three priority actions, and a live work ledger with owner, SLA, source, and next action.
options.risk: The briefing must stay operational and cannot become another passive dashboard.

raised.raise: Every summary fact opens the exact source work and preserves clinic scope.
Critical states change in place so staff never lose spatial orientation during a shift.

options.label: Exception Radar
options.lineage: A risk-first control surface for multi-clinic operations
options.thesis: Make exceptions—not routine activity—the dominant shape of the workspace.
options.viewport: A location matrix shows clinic readiness by schedule, calls, intake, staffing, and integrations; the selected exception expands into evidence and a safe action panel.
options.risk: A risk-led surface can feel alarmist unless normal and improving states remain legible.

options.label: Shift Timeline
options.lineage: A time-led operating view of the clinic day
options.thesis: Arrange work around what just happened, what is happening now, and what is likely to break next.
options.viewport: A horizontal now-line crosses appointments, calls, intake, staff coverage, and follow-ups; exceptions and handoffs attach to the exact moment they affect.
options.risk: Dense multi-location activity can overload the timeline without strong scope and progressive disclosure.
